entertainment.title: Daniel Hall, Co-Founder of Australian Rock Band Taxiride, Dies at 48
entertainment.summary: The guitarist and singer helped write and record “Get Set,” which won an ARIA Award and reached Billboard’s Modern Rock Tracks chart in 1999.
entertainment.body:
Daniel Hall , a co-founder of the Australian rock band Taxiride , died Friday (Nov. 13). He was 48.

The band announced his death in a social media post. “It is with the heaviest of hearts we announce the passing of our youngest brother in arms, Daniel James Hall,” it read. “We shared some amazing experiences and his departure doesn’t seem real. Rest In Peace Dan.”

In a separate post on Hall’s own page, his partner, Jess, said he died unexpectedly at home in the early hours of Friday. “I am completely devastated,” she wrote. “Your prayers and kind messages are appreciated.” No cause has been given. Related Karol G Surprises Mexico City Fans With Thalía as Special Guest: 'The First Person I Wanted to Be' Simple Plan, Hoobastank & More Take Warped Tour Mid-Flight Amid FAA Ground Stop Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Mid-Tour to Focus on His Health Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

Taxiride formed in Melbourne in the late ’90s, after Tim Watson and Tim Wild began writing together and were joined by Jason Singh and Hall, who had spent years busking in the suburb of Camberwell and playing Melbourne venues. The four-piece signed to Warner after recording a demo at the city’s Secret Sound Studios.

Their 1999 debut, Imaginate , produced by Jack Joseph Puig and recorded between Ocean Way in Los Angeles and Secret Sound, went to No. 1 on the ARIA albums chart and was certified double platinum in Australia . It was released in the U.S. on Warner/Sire.

Lead single “Get Set” reached No. 8 on the ARIA singles chart and No. 36 on Billboard’s Modern Rock Tracks chart, and won breakthrough artist – single at the 1999 ARIA Awards . It was also nominated for best pop release. Follow-up “Everywhere You Go” gave the band a second ARIA top 15 hit, and Imaginate drew two further ARIA nominations the following year.

Hall left Taxiride in 2001 to pursue solo work and later formed the band Airway Lanes. He subsequently returned to Taxiride, and the band has continued performing in Australia, with dates still in the diary at the time of his death.

Singh, his former bandmate, said he was “absolutely shattered.” Writing on social media, he said: “R.I.P. my brother Dan Hall. Forever in my soul. Thank you for being one of the hugest parts of my life brother. I’m totally heart broken.”

entertainment.title: Tearful Phil Collins receives electrifying ovation at Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony amid health battles
entertainment.summary: Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker inducted Collins into the Hall of Fame.
entertainment.body:
Phil Collins gave a tearful acceptance speech and got an electrifying tribute from Cynthia Erivo, Oprah Winfrey inducted the late Luther Vandross, and Wu-Tang Clan made the Peacock Theater a rowdy celebration at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night.

Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte and Sade were also inducted, and Billy Idol, New Order and Iron Maiden were set to enter the hall later in the evening.

Collins, whose mobility issues and other health problems kept him from performing , took the stage slowly using a pair of canes and cried at a huge ovation from a crowd that included his daughter, actor Lily Collins .

Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker inducted Collins and praised him for his unprecedented dual stardom as a drummer and a hit-making pop singer in the 1980s.

“I grew up just wanting to play the drums,” Collins said. “Everything else has been a really happy accident. I can’t believe, when I look back, how life has gone.”

Barker said Collins’ song “In the Air Tonight” gave the world “arguably the most badass drum fill of all time.”

Minutes later, Barker played that fill himself as Erivo gave a slowed-down, epic rendition of the song that brought the crowd to its feet.

Collins was already in the hall as a member of Genesis, but now gets the solo honor.

entertainment.title: ‘SNL’: Hippie John Mulaney Has Some Very Unhip Thoughts at Woodstock
entertainment.summary: Mulaney suggests how he and his baby boomer pals should live when they get older
entertainment.body:
On Saturday Night Live , Woodstock attendee John Mulaney shared with his hippie friends some very uncool ideas about how their generation should live when they’re older.

While listening to Sly and the Family Stone at the 1969 music festival , Mulaney suddenly blurts out to his pals an odd suggestion: “Hey, when we get older, I think we should buy all the houses.”

When a friend (Andrew Dismukes) expresses confusion, Mulaney explains: “Our generation, the baby boomers, when we get older, I think we should just buy as many houses as we can get, and just like, have them.”

His freinds (Sarah Sherman, Kenan Thompson and Mikey Day) are skeptical, while Mulaney insists that their spirit of generosity should flip “in fifteen years, like 1985 or so.” Then, he says, “we should become ruthless corporate climbers that absolutely fetishize money in an almost pornographic way. Far out, right?”

After he’s offered marijuana, Mulaney has another idea: “We should scare our kids about this stuff.”

The group objects, prompting Mulaney to explain: “I feel like in 1985—hey, there’s that year again, feel like it’s going to be a big year for us—we should tell our kids if they smoke weed even once, it’ll ruin their lives. And not just weed, everything.”

“Everything we should enjoy, we tell our kids that it will kill them stone-ass dead,” he says.

When a friend relies that only hard drugs should come with a warning, Mulaney responds: “No, we should make our kids do speed: ritalin, adderall, just shove it down their throats their entire childhood so they can get into college.”

entertainment.body:
U2 crashed the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night (Nov. 14), opening the show at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater with a surprise two-song set a day after releasing their new album, Carnaval De Luz . Explore U2 See latest videos, charts and news

The band weren’t on the bill — they were inducted back in 2005, their first year of eligibility — but they kicked off the night for a class that included Phil Collins , Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan. Related Karol G Surprises Mexico City Fans With Thalía as Special Guest: 'The First Person I Wanted to Be' Simple Plan, Hoobastank & More Take Warped Tour Mid-Flight Amid FAA Ground Stop Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Mid-Tour to Focus on His Health

They opened with “Silencio,” the album’s second single, joined by a line of performers dressed as riot police and carrying shields, then closed with “Pride (In the Name of Love),” a fixture of their live shows for four decades.

Carnaval De Luz , out Friday (Nov. 13) via Interscope, is U2 ’s 16th album and their first full-length of new material since 2017’s Songs of Experience . It was produced by longtime collaborator Jacknife Lee, and its title translates as “Carnival of Light.” The cover, showing the band walking single file along a beach with Bono out front in a top hat, is a clear nod to Abbey Road .

The album closes with “Torn,” a duet with Dolly Parton that her representative has confirmed is her final recorded vocal performance. Parton died in August at 80. U2 wrote the song with Parton and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, and have described it as a country song about broken family ties.

The release also gives U2 a shot at extending a Billboard 200 record. Songs of Experience was their eighth No. 1, making them the only group to top the chart in four consecutive decades. They’ve also notched two Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s, both from 1987’s The Joshua Tree . Carnaval De Luz ’s first-week numbers will be reflected on the Billboard 200 dated Nov. 28.

It’s been a busy 50th anniversary year for the band, who also released two six-song EPs, Days of Ash and Easter Lily , and played a surprise street show on Dublin’s Grafton Street in September. The Edge has called the new album “a messy, provocative, sacred collection of songs,” while Bono promised “loud guitars, deep bass, some ecstatic rhythms.”

entertainment.title: Richard Sterban, longtime bass singer for the Oak Ridge Boys, dead at 83
entertainment.summary: Ahead of joining the Oak Ridge Boys, Sterban worked as a backup singer for Elvis Presley.
entertainment.body:
Richard Sterban, longtime bass singer for the Grammy-winning Oak Ridge Boys, has died. He was 83.

Sterban died Saturday at his home in Hendersonville, Tenn., from complications of bronchitis and pneumonia following a long battle with cancer, according to a statement from his family and the band’s rep .

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers. Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus,” his family said in a statement.

Sterban was forced to step away from touring with the quartet in 2025 due to health issues, but reunited with the group in January 2026 to perform their 1981 hit “Elvira” at the Grand Ole Opry.

Born in 1943 in Camden, NJ, Sterban grew up in nearby Collingswood and began singing in Sunday school at age 6 as a soprano, before his voice dropped to the deep bass that became his trademark.

Sterban graduated from Collingswood High School and went on to study music at Trenton State College, now known as the College of New Jersey.

Sterban moved to Nashville in 1970, where he worked as a backup singer for Elvis Presley.

He left the job in 1972 to join the Oak Ridge Boys, alongside lead singer Duane Allen, baritone William Lee Golden and tenor Joe Bonsall.

entertainment.title: ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Roasts Trump Admin Over Grounded Flights, Jensen Huang Affairs

entertainment.body:
Saturday Night Live ‘s Weekend Update took aim at the Trump administration’s explanation for grounding all flights for hours on Friday, and questioned what the president knew about ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy .

“The scariest part about all these flights getting grounded was the messaging from the normally dependable Trump administration,” Colin Jost began. “First, they said it was a ‘telecommunications outage, as of now.’ Why add ‘as of now?’ No one wants to hear: ‘Your child is safe, as of now.'”

“Then, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said the whole situation was the result of a contractor upgrading copper wire to fiberoptic cable. So, one guy switched out one wire and took out all planes? I think that’s literally a scene from the movie, ‘Airplane!'” Jost joked.

Co-anchor Michael Che turned to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin telling reporters in the early stage of the incident that it was not a 9/11-type situation.

“Which he knew, because Rudy Giuliani didn’t see his shadow,” he joked.

Jost then addressed ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affairs, some reportedly with his subordinates and one with a suspected Chinese spy. The news has caused stocks to fall, since the company’s A.I. chips are shouldering a large part of the U.S. economy.

“Jensen Huang had a midlife crisis so bad, you might lose your house in his divorce,” he joked.

Jost then addressed the uncertainty about what Donald Trump knew about Huang potentially being taken advantage of and when he knew it.

entertainment.title: Phil Collins Tells Rock Hall Crowd: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me’
entertainment.summary: Travis Barker inducted the Genesis frontman as a solo artist, while Cynthia Erivo performed “In the Air Tonight” in his place.
entertainment.body:
Phil Collins was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist on Saturday (Nov. 14), and used his acceptance speech to tell the crowd he isn’t done yet. Explore Cynthia Erivo Genesis Phil Collins See latest videos, charts and news

“You haven’t heard the last of me,” Collins said during the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. “I promise you that.” Related Karol G Surprises Mexico City Fans With Thalía as Special Guest: 'The First Person I Wanted to Be' Simple Plan, Hoobastank & More Take Warped Tour Mid-Flight Amid FAA Ground Stop Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Mid-Tour to Focus on His Health

The honor marks Collins’ second induction. He entered the Hall in 2010 as a member of Genesis , making him one of a small number of two-time inductees.

Travis Barker inducted Collins, highlighting his impact as a drummer. “I remember hearing the drums for the first time and being blown away,” the Blink-182 drummer said of “In the Air Tonight.” “That sound changed everything. It helped define the sound of drums in the eighties, and you can still hear Phil’s influence today.”

Barker also pointed to Collins’ success with both Genesis and his solo career. “He wasn’t just successful at both,” he said, “he was one of the best at both.”

Collins did not perform at the ceremony. He said earlier this year that he had declined an invitation to play because he wasn’t “match-fit” enough to rehearse and sing properly, though he did not rule out returning to the stage. Cynthia Erivo performed “In the Air Tonight” in his place, with Barker on drums.

In his speech, Collins said he felt unprepared following a night of more polished addresses, and opened by telling the audience he’s “really not as bad as it looks.” He said his career began with a single goal: “I grew up wanting to play drums. Everything else has been a happy accident.”

Collins credited his assistant with saving his life, saying he needed to name her despite her dislike of attention. “I’m not joking when I say without her I wouldn’t be here,” he said. “I’d be in a box six feet under.” He said she had told him what he was doing was bad for him and what to do about it, adding that he’s “a well man now.”

entertainment.title: ‘SNL’ Cold Open: Jensen Huang, Tech CEOs Get a Crash Course in Female Spies
entertainment.summary: Bowen Yang returns to SNL to play the ousted Nvidia CEO, who gives advice to Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg and others
entertainment.body:
Saturday Night Live opened with host John Mulaney instructing a naive group of tech leaders how to tell whether a woman is genuinely interested in them or is a spy trying to extract valuable information from them, as may be the case with ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang .

Mulaney, as a CIA officer, summons Peter Thiel (James Austin Johnson), Sam Altman (Ben Marshall), Dario Amodei (Jane Wickline), Mark Zuckerberg (Andrew Dismukes) and Elon Musk (Jeremy Culhane) to agency headquarters to brief them on a matter of national security.

“America needs you to learn the difference between a woman who would actually want to have sex with you, and a woman who is clearly a spy,” Mulaney says. He then asks the group what the lesson in Huang’s downfall is.

“Never date anyone, lest they become the antichrist,” Thiel says.

Mulaney then tries using a Venn diagram to get his point across. The diagram shows two circles that do not overlap one bit: “beautiful women” and “your interests and opinions.”

“So,” he asks the group, “if someone is both of these things, then they are a what?”

When informed that this person would be a spy, Musk goes on one of his unfunny tangents about James Bond, prompting Mulaney to squirt him with a water bottle to get him to shut up.

Logo text Bowen Yang made a surprise appearance on Saturday Night Live to portray former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to warn a group of tech billionaires about how to decipher between “a woman who would actually want to have sex with you and a woman who is clearly a spy.”

John Mulaney , who served as the host of the episode, kicked off the cold open by welcoming the group of moguls, including Sam Altman (Ben Marshall), Peter Thiel (James Austin Johnson), Elon Musk (Jeremy Culhane), Mark Zuckerberg (Andrew Dismukes) and Dario Amodei (Jane Wickline). entertainment.title: BTS & ROSÉ Lead a Big Night for K-Pop at 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards: Full Winners List
entertainment.summary: Bruno Mars won favorite male artist for the second year in a row. Sombr and KATSEYE took the "breakout" awards.
entertainment.body:
Kids love K-Pop. That was abundantly clear from the results at the 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards, which aired on CBS for the first time on Saturday (Nov. 14). BTS won three major awards, though they weren’t at Television City in Hollywood for the taping, nor did they accept any of their awards by video, as ROSÉ and “global girl group” KATSEYE did.

BTS won favorite group for a record-extending fifth time; favorite song (“Swim”) for a second time and favorite album ( ARIRANG ) for the first time. In the favorite song category, BTS had won five years ago for “Dynamite.” The only other group or duo to win twice in the category is One Direction (back-to-back awards in 2013-14 for “What Makes You Beautiful” and “Story of My Life”). (The Kids’ Choice Awards originated in 1987.)

ROSÉ became the first K-Pop star to win favorite female artist. She beat, among others, Ariana Grande, who has won a record five times in this category; Taylor Swift, who has won three times; and Miley Cyrus, who has won twice.

ROSÉ’s Blackpink colleague JENNIE shared the award for favorite music collaboration with Tame Impala for their smash “Dracula.”

KPop Demon Hunters also won multiple awards. “Golden” won favorite song from a movie (beating Swift’s “I Knew It, I Knew You” from Toy Story 5 , among others). The actors who voiced Rumi and Jinu in that movie won for favorite female and male animated voices from a movie, respectively.

Alex Warren was a good-natured host of the fast-paced show, which ran just 90 minutes. In one quick bit, he was costumed like a janitor, mopping up the slime. Only a dozen of the many awards were presented on the show. The producers program the show with the winners who were willing and able to appear. If you watched the show, you would have had no idea that BTS had a big night.

Nor would you have known that Bruno Mars won favorite male artist for the second year in a row; that Sombr won favorite new male artist; or that Olivia Dean ‘s “Man I Need” took favorite viral song. “Man I Need” is expected to be a top contender for record and song of the year at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

KATSEYE won favorite female breakout artist/group. Bini , a Filipino girl group, won favorite global music star.

entertainment.body: Journey is pushing ahead with its Final Frontier Tour following the departure of the band's longtime drummer, Deen Castronovo. "After careful consideration and an extensive year of touring, our talented, longtime drummer Deen Castronovo has decided to step away to focus on personal health matters that require his attention," the "Open Arms" band revealed via a Friday, November 13, statement. "He has our full support during this time and extends his heartfelt thanks to the fans for the love, encouragement, and kindness he has received." The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees have enlisted fill-in drummer Steve Murphy for the remainder of this year's dates on Journey's farewell tour. "Native New Yorker Steve Murphy who comes to us from working with bands such as Alan Parsons Project, Trans Siberian Orchestra, Christopher Cross and Jack Bruce will be joining us for the remainder of November," the band confirmed via Instagram. "We look forward to continuing to share unforgettable nights of music with all of you." Castronovo's shocking departure from Journey follows two recent incidents where he had to exit the stage mid-performance, forcing his bandmates to rearrange their show on the fly, with drum tech Steve Toomey ultimately filling in on both occasions. entertainment.title: Phil Collins, 75, makes rare public appearance with daughter Lily amid yearslong health battles
entertainment.summary: The "You'll Be in My Heart" singer retired from performing in 2022.
entertainment.body:
Phil Collins made a rare public appearance at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday evening.

The “You’ll Be in My Heart” crooner, 75, was photographed wearing a classic tux while walking with two canes down the red carpet.

Phil was joined by three of his five children for the joyous occasion, including “Emily in Paris” star Lily Collins, his middle child.

He was also pictured with daughter Joely Collins and son Nicholas “Nic” Collins.

Phil is among the elite group receiving music’s highest honor this year in the performer category, alongside the likes of Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan.

In a statement shared to his Instagram page earlier Saturday, Phil reflected on what being inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame means to him, saying he’s “glad it’s happened now.”

“I always appreciated it and I always realised that I was lucky to have that kind of success, but when it actually happens, it’s a pat on the back, it’s like ‘you done good,’” he continued. “I was thrilled because I’d turned 75 this year and I thought, ‘It’s all coming together at a certain time.’”

Phil said he was “pleased and honored” when he was announced as an inductee in April, per a statement he shared to his Instagram at the time.

entertainment.body: Chicago Fire actress Robyn Coffin is expected to undergo surgery after being diagnosed with breast cancer. "Robyn has been diagnosed with breast cancer. Terrible news," a statement on her GoFundMe page read. "The good news – she has a crack team at the hospital organizing and planning her surgery and aftercare and recovery." Coffin set up the fundraising page with friend Gianine DeFrancesco in hopes of supporting the actress through her upcoming operation and recovery. An initial fundraising goal has been set at $75,000, with more than $15,000 already raised as of publication. "When Robyn doesn’t work, she doesn’t get paid," DeFrancesco clarfied via GoFundMe. "So, this go fund me is not only to fill in the gaps that insurance will surely leave, but also to help sustain Robyn and [her husband] Grant while Robyn is off work. Thank goodness they have insurance, but let’s not get cocky – let’s give them a nest egg because we know there will be surprises." Coffin is expected to have a right partial mastectomy with magseed localization on December 3, followed by a course of radiation. First, she will meet with her care team on November 24 to make a final decision on whether a partial or full mastectomy will be the best treatment option. "If that visit results in affirming the right partial mastectomy, Robyn is expecting to be out of work for 3 weeks," DeFrancesco explained. "If a full mastectomy is required, Robyn’s time off work will increase quite a bit, as the surgery is much more extensive." Fans were assured in the fundraising appeal that Coffin will be able to count on her "husband Grant and supportive friends [as] wonderful caregivers." "We know that with insurance the surgery and hospital bill will amount to $40k. Because the surgery is hard upon, this amount is most urgent. "So, Village – thank you in advance for embracing Robyn with love and support. We’ve got her!" Based on Robyn Carr’s book series, Virgin River follows the lives of residents living in a small town in Northern California, including Mel (Alexandra Breckenridge) and Jack (Martin Henderson). The hit series, which premiered in 2019, also stars Colin Lawrence, Annette O'Toole, Tim Matheson, Benjamin Hollingsworth, Sarah Dugdale, Zibby Allen and Kai Bradbury. After seven seasons, there have been some major departures from the Netflix show. Grayson Gurnsey left as Ricky after season 4, and Mark Ghanimé, who played Cameron, had a surprising exit once season 6 was released. "I think this season saw a little bit of a sendoff for Cameron," showrunner Patrick Sean Smith exclusively told Us Weekly in December 2024. "In terms of Mark, the actor who I adore, he unfortunately won't be coming back for season 7." Smith didn't rule out a potential return for the character in the future. "But that's not to say that Cameron's not a part of our world forever," he added. "I would love to bring him back, and bring his character back when the story presents itself.” In March 2026, Virgin River returned for season 7, and it was later confirmed that Marco Grazzini will not reprise his role as Mike. In another twist, Lauren Hammersley, who has played Charmaine since the show premiered, is also not expected to come back for season 8. “For me, I’m just trying to look [at] the longevity of the show and making sure that the characters that we’re keeping have enough story engine in them to keep going,” Smith told Deadline at the time. “So I can’t say there are any specific cast shakeups planned, but I think we will have to start to — as characters run their course — make some decisions and bring in some new blood.” The show was renewed for season 9 before season 8 premiered on Netflix. Bhutan, South Korea, Mongolia, Nepal, Cambodia and Bangladesh also competed.

Contestants made their entrances aboard tuk-tuks, the motorized three-wheeled vehicles common in Bangkok’s tourist districts. They waved national flags as thousands of fans cheered inside the city-center venue.

Sitcom fans may recognize her from " The Big Bang Theory ," where she played Beverly Hofstadter, Leonard's (Johnny Galecki) analytical psychiatrist mother. She appeared on the sitcom on and off for more than a decade, but her longest-running role was in a different CBS franchise.

She played the character until the show's end in 2016, but that wasn't the last viewers saw of Diane. Baranski reprised the role as the protagonist of the spin-off "The Good Fight," which ran for six seasons from 2017 to 2022.

Baranski's history with CBS goes back to 1995 and the Chuck Lorre sitcom "Cybill," in which she played the titular character's best friend. It was also her first role as a series regular. From there, Baranski landed main roles in "Welcome to New York" and "Happy Family." Her TV credits also include various voice roles and guest appearances on "Law & Order," "Frasier," "Ugly Betty," and "Psych," among others.

Universal Pictures Before making a name for herself on TV, Christine Baranski studied performing arts at Juilliard, graduating in 1974. She went on to appear in numerous Broadway productions, winning Tony Awards for her performances in the plays "The Real Thing" and "Rumors" before joining the original cast of the musical "Nick & Nora." Her stage background also carried over into several movie musicals.

Among her best-known films are the jukebox musicals "Mamma Mia!" and its sequel, "Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again," both featuring music by ABBA. In both films, Baranski played Tanya, a friend of Meryl Streep's Donna. She also portrayed the Stepmother in Disney's movie musical adaptation of Stephen Sondheim's "Into the Woods" and had a supporting role in "Chicago."

entertainment.title: Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys Bass Singer Who Helped Make ‘Elvira’ a Hit, Dies at 83
entertainment.summary: Known for his signature "oom poppa, mow mow" bass line on "Elvira," Sterban had 17 No. 1s on the Hot Country Songs chart with The Oak Ridge Boys, plus two top 40 hits on the all-genre Hot 100.
entertainment.body:
Richard Sterban, the bass vocalist behind the “oom poppa, mow mow” hook on one of The Oak Ridge Boys ‘ biggest hits, “Elvira,” and whose career launched as a backing singer for Elvis Presley , died on Saturday (Nov. 14). He was 83.

Sterban passed away due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia in Hendersonville, Tenn., his family shared. He died after a long battle with cancer, and after retiring from touring last year.

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers,” the Sterban family said in a statement released on Saturday. “Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time. We find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus.”

Sterban, a member of The Oak Ridge Boys for more than 50 years with Duane Allen, William Lee Golden and the late Joe Bonsall, revealed a pancreatic cancer diagnosis in September 2025 , saying at the time that he was “under the care of the best cancer doctors in the country and, with the help of the Good Lord above, I believe I will be able to get through this.”

“Elvira” — The Oak Ridge Boys’ highest-charting single on the all-genre Billboard Hot 100, a song that became one of the quartet’s numerous No. 1s on the Hot Country Songs chart, and the winner of a trio of major awards (a Grammy Award, a CMA Award and an ACM Award) put Sterban’s deep vocal front and center in the hit’s chorus.

The Oak Ridge Boys had 47 entries on the Hot Country Songs chart, including 17 No. 1s that spanned 1978-90. They also had 39 entries on the Top Country Albums chart, including three No. 1s ( Fancy Free in 1981, Bobbie Sue in 1982 and Deliver in 1984). On the all-genre Billboard Hot 100, the group notched four entries, including two top 40-charted hits: “Elvira” (No. 5 in 1981) and “Bobbie Sue” (No. 12 in 1982).

Sterban was born in Camden, N.J., in 1934, and grew up in nearby Collingswood, where he sang at Sunday school and in his seventh grade glee club. He went to Trenton State College, now The College of New Jersey, to study music.

Before his professional journey in music led him to The Oak Ridge Boys, Sterban helped found the gospel quartet The Keystones in the Philadelphia area; Bonsall, who would go on to join The Oak Ridge Boys with him, also sang in the group.

Fishel remembered crying about Jacobs’ alleged comments, which she said triggered a yearlong struggle with eating.

entertainment.title: Long Before Lioness, Morgan Freeman Was In Nearly 800 Episodes Of An Iconic '70s Kids Show
entertainment.summary: One of Hollywood's most legendary actors, Morgan Freeman was relatively unknown when he starred on an educational kids show in the 1970s.
entertainment.body:
From 1971 to 1977, "The Electric Company" was one of the shows that helped educate Generation X . With a blend of colorful characters, upbeat songs, recurring sketches, and a sense of humor, the show educated children on the finer points of grammar and reading. Aimed at kids who had outgrown "Sesame Street," the show become immensely popular and ran for 780 episodes. And for every one of those episodes, Freeman was there playing a wide range of characters.

Among his most popular recurring characters was the Mad Scientist, who tried reading words associated with his experiments. There was also Mel Mounds, a DJ who would introduce various songs, and Easy Reader, a groovy character who would sing and dance while reading sentences out loud. Those appearances were a far cry from his role on "Lioness," where he spends much of the show dealing with an undercover group of female CIA operatives, but they did lay the groundwork for his expansive and long-reaching career.

PBS / YouTube While Morgan Freeman is currently enjoying success on "Lioness," a show he's praised for its courageous writing , he was a relative unknown when he debuted on "The Electric Company." However, several of his castmates had already established themselves as big stars. Rita Moreno, who like Freeman also appeared in all 780 episodes, had won an Oscar for "West Side Story" 10 years before "The Electric Company" was released.

"The Electric Company" also managed to attract top talent as guest stars. Joan Rivers, Gene Wilder, and Zero Mostel all lent their voices to the recurring animated feature "The Adventures of Letterman," and Mel Brooks voiced a cartoon character who would read words as he walked on-screen. Later on they even struck a deal with Marvel to bring another famous name to the show: Spider-Man. "Spidey Super Stories" used on-screen speech balloons to help children to read. Cast members would take turns narrating the segments, including Freeman, who has since become one of the world's most prominent narrators.

Even the writers' room was loaded with talent. Thad Mumford, who won an Emmy writing for "The Electric Company," would later go on to write for "M*A*S*H." Jeremy Stevens, meanwhile, would go on to write for several sitcoms including "Coach" and "Everybody Loves Raymond."

entertainment.summary: "Gilligan's Island" star Bob Denver showed off his versatility by playing no less than four different characters on "Fantasy Island."
entertainment.body:
Like his fellow castaways, Bob Denver will forever be associated with "Gilligan's Island." Although Denver reprised his Gilligan character numerous times, including on a crossover episode of the 1980s' hit "ALF," he also got to play other roles during that decade. In particular, Denver guest-starred on "Fantasy Island," taking on four different characters between 1980 and 1983.

Unlike the never-rescued "Gilligan's Island" castaways , "Fantasy Island" visitors were able to get off their tropical paradise island after a brief stay. For his first appearance in Season 3's "Eagleman," Denver played Morris Binstock, a man who wants to become a literal superhero dad. His comedic skills make him perfect for the role, which involves a whimsical feathered costume. Everything goes according to plan, until Denver appears in this disguise in front of his boss, played by his former "Gilligan's" co-star, Jim Backus.

In Season 5's "House of Dolls," things start to take on a "Twilight Zone"-like vibe. Denver plays Francis Elkins, a lonely window dresser who gets his wish for a mannequin to come to life (a few years before the famous '80s film "Mannequin" had a similar plot point). An episode later, Denver's back in "The Magic Camera" as photography enthusiast Don Winters, who discovers both the ups and downs of a future-predicting camera and begs for an early departure from the island.

Denver makes a final appearance in the Season 6 episode "Love Island" as middle school science teacher Tim Kearns, who's wearing a bright orange hat similar to Gilligan's signature headgear. While looking for love, Kearns and his buddy are surprised by some cheesy stop-motion dinos.

ABC Surprisingly, "Fantasy Island" reportedly began as a joke . As executive producer Aaron Spelling recounted in his memoir, "Aaron Spelling: A Prime-Time Life," he was frustrated during a brainstorming session with ABC TV execs. "I said, 'You guys don't want a show. You don't want something with characters or a plot or a story. You just want to have some sort of an island, where you can go and act out all your dumb fantasies." To Spelling's shock, he accidentally hit the nail on the head.

This premise turned out to be a boon for the series' many guest stars, since each episode starts out with new people being welcomed to the island to live out their requests. Due to those outsized casting demands, the show has a repertory feel, with Bob Denver being one of many actors who were asked to make repeat appearances. Before he and Denver reunited on "Fantasy Island," Jim Backus also appeared on the first season. Out of the other "Gilligan's Island" alums, Alan Hale Jr. had three guest roles, and Dawn Wells and Tina Louise each had one.

entertainment.title: Morgan Freeman And James Earl Jones Led An All-Star Cast In This True-Crime Miniseries
entertainment.summary: Back in the 1980s, Morgan Freeman and James Earl Jones starred in a gripping two-part dramatization of the infamous Atlanta Child Murders case.
entertainment.body:
Airing in two parts in February 1985, "The Atlanta Child Murders" dramatized the investigation into more than two dozen murders of Black children and adults that occurred in Georgia's capital from 1979 to 1981. Freeman and Jones both played fictional composite characters, a detective and chief of police, respectively. Other actors, like Rip Torn, Martin Sheen, Jason Robards, and Gloria Foster, played real people. Bill Paxton also played a memorable role .

The second half of the five-hour miniseries focused on the trial of Wayne Williams (Calvin Levels), who in 1982 was convicted of murdering two adult victims. He wasn't convicted of any additional crimes, but the authorities were able to link Williams to a further 19 murders. The killings stopped after Williams was apprehended, though there are those who doubt his guilt.

"The Atlanta Child Murders" screenwriter Abby Mann told The New York Times he didn't "believe Wayne Williams's guilt was proven" and that he wanted viewers to question the prosecution and alleged breaches of legal ethics. Freeman himself told The Washington Post that he thought "one person was not responsible for all of the killings." Atlanta officials accused the show of being irresponsibly loose with facts, and CBS agreed to add a disclaimer saying parts of the narrative were fictionalized.

Netflix The Atlanta murders and the lingering doubts following Wayne Williams' conviction have been dramatized several times. In 2000, Showtime aired a TV movie titled "Who Killed Atlanta's Children?" It stars James Belushi and Gregory Hines as two journalists who reported on a conspiracy that the Ku Klux Klan committed the murders and framed Williams.

In 2019, the murders were the main focus of the second season of "Mindhunter," one of the best Netflix shows based on true stories . "You could probably do three seasons on the Atlanta Child Murders," showrunner David Fincher said on KCRW's "The Treatment" podcast. "It's a huge and sweeping and tragic story. We couldn't do it justice in the background of our nine hours."

That same year, Atlanta police reopened the case hoping that advancements in DNA technology would allow them to make a new breakthrough, and in 2020, HBO premiered "Atlanta's Missing and Murdered: The Lost Children," a five-part documentary series focused on the crime and new evidence. It's one of several great true crime shows streaming on HBO Max .

sports.title: 49ers will fly to Colorado tonight to begin acclimating to altitude for Mexico City game
sports.summary: The 49ers won't fly home after today's game in Dallas.
sports.body:
The team plane will fly to Colorado Springs tonight, as coach Kyle Shanahan believes spending a week at altitude will help the 49ers’ chances against the Vikings next week at Estadio Azteca, the highest stadium the NFL ever plays in.

“I think it helps,” Shanahan said. “I grew up mainly in Denver, and I know how bad it would be for me. No matter how good of shape you’re in, you come home from college and you run up the stairs and you’re out of breath. It takes some time to get used to altitude. I know when you go to play in Denver it’s always a challenge, and Mexico City is higher than Denver. It’s not make or break, but I do think it makes you a couple percent better.”

Shanahan thanked Air Force head coach Troy Calhoun for allowing the 49ers to use his team’s practice facility in Colorado Springs, as he did before the 49ers’ Mexico City game in 2022. Air Force’s Falcon Stadium is at 6,621 feet. Estadio Azteca has an altitude of 7,280 feet — exactly 2,000 feet higher than Denver’s Mile High elevation.

Next Sunday night will be the 49ers’ second international game of the season. They opened the season in Australia, where their decision to arrive a week early to get used to the time difference was credited as one of the reasons for their impressive performance against the Rams. Now they hope another weeklong preparation will yield similar results.

sports.title: Arch Manning shakes off 3 interceptions, throws game-winning TD pass as Texas beats LSU
sports.summary: As he has been throughout his college football career, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was a mixed bag on Saturday.
sports.body:
After throwing three interceptions and seeing his team fall behind LSU 21-10, Manning turned it on late, culminating in a 12-play, 58-yard drive that saw Manning throw the game-winning touchdown pass with three seconds remaining as Texas won 22-21.

“That’s what college football is all about,” Manning said after the game.

Manning’s numbers were not impressive: 19-of-35 for 174 yards and one touchdown with three interceptions and four sacks, plus 35 yards and a touchdown running. But when Texas needed him to march the offense down the field at the end of the game, he did it. His touchdown pass to Raleek Brown was a perfectly placed ball, and he also ran for two first downs on the game-winning drive.

For No. 6 Texas, the win means they’ll almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, as they’ll be heavy favorites the next two weeks against Arkansas and Texas A&M. For LSU, the loss knocks first-year coach Lane Kiffin out of playoff contention.

Manning, the scion of the first family of quarterbacks, will have an opportunity do what neither his grandfather Archie nor his uncles Peyton and Eli ever did: Win a national championship.

sports.title: Lions, Jets renegotiated Andre Cisco trade after concerns arose about his physical
sports.summary: The Broncos-Chargers Daiyan Henley trade wasn't the only one affected by the player's physical.
sports.body:
The Lions also told the Jets they wanted to change the terms of their trade for safety Andre Cisco after concerns about his physical. But unlike the Chargers, the Jets agreed to it, and the Lions ultimately sent the Jets a 2029 sixth-round pick for Cisco after initially agreeing to give up a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Tom Pelissero reports that the modified terms were based on medical concerns. There’s no word on what those concerns were, but Lions coach Dan Campbell said the plan is for Cisco to play on Sunday against the Patriots.

The Jets went along with the Lions’ request, and in the scheme of things the difference between a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 sixth-round pick is minor. Still, it points to an inherent flaw in the NFL’s trade rules: The team acquiring a player has the ability to go back on the trade, or negotiate better terms, after the trade deadline. That puts the team trading the player in a difficult position: After you’ve already told a player you’re trading him, and told another player you’re signing him or bringing him up from the practice squad to take his place, you don’t want to go back on that. So if the team you’re trading with tells you, “We didn’t like his physical, so we’ll back out of the trade unless you take less compensation,” you may feel you have no choice but to accept.

The NFL could resolve that by not allowing trades to be renegotiated after the deadline: Either the player passes the physical and the trade goes through, or the player fails the physical and the trade does not go through. No more half measures like, “We failed him on his physical, but we’ll pass the physical if you agree to take a lesser draft pick for him.”

Another solution could be that physicals for traded players are conducted by an independent, league-appointed doctor, rather than the team’s medical staff. If that doctor says the player passes the physical, the team trading for the player can’t back out.

The Jets and Chargers had different reactions to their trade partners asking to renegotiate the trades, but the situation both teams were faced with highlights potential problems that can arise with the NFL allowing teams to change the terms of trades after the trade deadline.

On Saturday morning, the NFL announced that three non-referees will serve as referees for four Week 10 games, with one of them — Don Willard — working as the referee for the 1:00 p.m. ET game between the Dolphins and Colts before traveling to Cincinnati for Sunday night’s Steelers-Bengals game.

The reconfiguration resulted from the NFL’s decision to assign officials to games within driving distance of their homes.

Austro also notes that the replay officials for all Sunday games will work out of NFL headquarters. They were in Detroit on Friday for an all-day, in-person training session. Instead of fanning out to the various game locations, they all went to New York.

It sets the stage for a potentially strange day, with any mistakes inevitably being blamed on the inability of the NFL to get the officials where they needed to be. If it works, however, it could prompt the NFL to reconsider the overall staffing plan, if there’s a way to do it that reduces expenses.

I think that’s a tongue-in-cheek remark. I hope it’s a tongue-in-cheek remark.

Either way, Sunday could get interesting. The players and coaches have gotten to where they’re supposed to be. The officials haven’t, and the deck has been dramatically reshuffled in order to ensure that each game will be properly staffed.

sports.title: Game between Bill Belichick's UNC and Louisville ends in a brawl
sports.summary: Saturday's not alright for fighting.
sports.body:
But a fight nevertheless happened at the end of the game between Louisville and Bill Belichick’s North Carolina Tar Hells.

The Cardinals led, 16-14, with time ticking away. (UNC had a timeout remaining but hadn’t used it on the final Louisville drive, after a game-sealing interception.) Louisville received the snap and took a knee as the clock hit 15 seconds.

North Carolina, despite not using its final timeout, deployed the Schiano-style effort to blow up victory formation. Which sparked a shoving match match between opposing lineman. Which eventually became a full-blown brawl.

Through it all, time expired and the game ended. It will be interesting to see whether the ACC or the individual schools hand out suspensions as a result of the fracas.

The loss dropped North Carolina to 5-5. The Tar Heels need one win in remaining games against Virginia and NC State to become bowl-eligible in Belichick’s second season on the job.

And that could be harder to do against Virginia next week, if one or more UNC players end up being required to sit out.

He graduated from the University of Hawaii and spent time with the San Antonio Brahmas in the USFL prior to signing a futures contract with the Jets in 2025. sports.title: NFL tells Senator that Jalen Hurts review will include "mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts"
sports.summary: Five weeks since Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts played a game in London with a blood clot in his leg, the NFL and NFL Players Association have not yet begun an official investigation of the situation.
sports.body:
As noted on Friday by Tim McManus of ESPN, the league and the union are still working “ to hammer out [the] parameters ” of the investigation.

That has not stopped the NFL from providing some preliminary information to Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), who previously expressed concerns about the situation in a letter to the league.

“As outlined by the league and NFLPA’s Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties,” NFL executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement that was released by Blunt Rochester’s office on Friday.

It’s still unclear how the investigation will proceed or what it will entail. The NFLPA has not yet invoked its absolute right to launch an investigation under Article 39 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement as the communications with the league continue.

The ensuing delay is approaching the status of “head scratching.” With games being played every Thursday, Sunday, and Monday, there’s a constant risk of a similar situation arising. The sooner the Hurts situation is properly explored and any lessons learned from it are put into action, the sooner all players will benefit from any enhanced protections.

The Eagles and the league created widespread skepticism regarding whether a coverup is happening. (The NFL may not appreciate that being said, but that doesn’t make the perception inaccurate.) The NFLPA can’t afford to be viewed as being complicit in an effort to sweep the incident under the rug.

Through it all, the most effective investigative process comes from litigation, an adversarial process aimed at getting to the truth. However it happens as to Hurts, the only goal should be getting to the truth about why it all happened — and how it can be prevented from happening again.

They have signed kicker Zane Gonzalez to the active roster from the practice squad. They also elevated quarterback Brady Cook and wide receiver Jalen Reagor from the practice squad on a temporary basis.

sports.title: Steelers say Pat Freiermuth is questionable for Sunday night vs. Bengals with an illness
sports.summary: The Steelers might be without tight end Pat Freiermuth on Sunday night against the Bengals.
sports.body:
Freiermuth has been added to the Steelers’ injury report with an illness. He is listed as questionable.

Freiermuth has started all eight games for the Steelers this season. He has 25 catches for 235 yards and leads the team with four receiving touchdowns. The Steelers love using their two tight ends in the red zone; seven of Aaron Rodgers’ 13 touchdown passes this season have gone to either Freiermuth or tight end Darnell Washington.

The Steelers use a lot of two-tight end formations; Freiermuth has played 65.5 percent of the Steelers’ offensive snaps this season and Washington has played 64.7 percent. If Freiermuth can’t go, backup Robert Tonyan will likely get more playing time.

sports.title: Packers, Broncos explored possible Tony Pollard trade
sports.summary: One week before the trade deadline, teams had interest in Titans running back Tony Pollard.
sports.body:
Via ESPNFL, the Packers and Broncos “ checked in ” on Pollard. The Titans wouldn’t move Pollard for less than a third-round pick.

Both teams had been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The Colts, after creating the impression that Taylor would be traded, opted to take the best offer they could get.

The fact that Green Bay and Denver explored acquiring two different tailbacks isn’t much of a vote of confidence in their current depth charts. As to the Packers, it underscores the potentially tenuous status of Josh Jacobs.

Pollard, a fourth-round pick of the Cowboys in 2019, started his career as the backup/understudy to Ezekiel Elliott. Pollard had a breakthrough season in 2022, rushing for 1,007 yards and making it to the Pro Bowl despite Elliott still being the starter. (Elliott gained 876 yards that season.)

Pollard became the full-time starter in 2023, a franchise-tag season. He signed with the Titans in 2024.

He has four straight 1,000-yard seasons. Through eight games in 2026, he has 595 yards. Which puts him on pace for what would be a career-high 1,190 yards.

Pollard is in the final year of a three-year, $21.75 million contract. He’s due to be a free agent in March.

Walker leads the league, averaging 109.0 rushing yards per game. He’s tallied a total of 872 yards with seven rushing touchdowns in eight games. He’s also caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four TDs.

Johnson has 111 rushing yards on 26 carries with a touchdown and 14 receptions for 237 yards with a TD so far this year.

sports.body: The Jets’ defense has had its issues in 2026, to say the least. However, there’s at least one area where they have improved. The defense as a whole has been a lot more opportunistic this year in terms of forcing fumbles. Led by David Bailey’s five, they have forced a total of 13 fumbles. That’s already four more than the total for all of last season. New York’s fumble luck has been a lot better too, as they’ve recovered 50 percent of all fumbles. This is much higher than their 2025 percentage, which was the second-worst in the league at 35 percent (and was actually on target to break the all-time record until they had a few over the last few weeks of the season). Had they been closer to 50 percent last year, or 2023 when they were dead last in fumble recovery percentage, or 2022 when they were 30th, those seasons could arguably have played out very differently. 2023 in particular was particularly galling, as the Jets started 7-4 and then lost their last six as the turnovers dried up. They almost tied the all-time NFL record for the fewest defensive fumble recoveries until Carl Lawson ended a nine-game drought by recovering one with two games remaining. In the end, they only managed to recover 21 percent of fumbles by opposing offenses. It’s often been debated how much of fumble recovery percentages are dictated by talent and how much is based on luck, with most analytical studies concluding it’s mostly luck. However, if you have a team that is hungry and hustles to the ball, has players who are particularly adept at possessing loose balls or are creating the kinds of fumbles which are more likely to be recovered by the defense, this obviously has an effect on some level. sports.title: Jared Goff takes 1-3 career record vs. Patriots into Germany game
sports.summary: For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter.
sports.body:
Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That’s a 25-percent win rate.

In those four games, Goff has two touchdown passes and five interceptions.

Sunday’s game in Germany will be the first one against the Patriots with a coach other than Bill Belichick. Goff has never faced current Patriots coach Mike Vrabel; during Goff’s time as a starter with the Rams and Lions and Vrabel’s tenure with the Titans, their two teams never crossed paths.

Goff’s first loss to New England came in 2016, in his third career start. The Patriots won, 26-10. Two years later, New England beat Goff and the Rams in the Super Bowl, 13-3.

In 2020, Goff and the Rams beat the Patriots, 24-3. In 2022, the Patriots beat Goff and the Lions, 29-0.

Sunday’s game is consequential for both teams. The 6-2 Lions are caught in a cluster of four NFC North teams that all have six or more wins. The Patriots, at 5-4, are fading in the AFC East race and could be scrambling to secure a wild-card spot.

It’s just the second divisional game for the Bills, as they have just their October loss vs. the New England Patriots on their AFC East ledger so far. The Jets, meanwhile, will finish their first go-rounds of AFC East games with Sunday’s matchup. While New York may be just 2-7 this season, they’ve played a lot of tight games, including two against the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins. The Patriots defeated the Jets 26-19, while the Dolphins squeaked out a 28-25 victory. Really, the only game the Jets were entirely demolished in came last week, when they lost 35-12 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Can the Jets play the Bills tight this week? Will Buffalo overlook their division rivals and lose the game outright? There’s no question that Buffalo is the better football team, but there’s a reason why they play the games rather than just talking about them. The Bills will need to come out ready to roll in order to maintain their hold on the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Here are five Bills to watch on Sunday as they try to do just that. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen Last week, after a slow start, Allen caught fire in the second half against an outstanding Minnesota Vikings defense. sports.body: The Jets recently signed former Colts offensive lineman Blake Freeland to their active roster from the Bengals’ practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 25-year old Freeland is listed at 6’7” and 302 pounds and was a fourth round pick out of BYU in 2023. He has started nine games in his career, all of which were for the Colts in his rookie year. Background Freeland was a three-star high school recruit but headed to BYU with zero experience of playing on the offensive line having been a quarterback for two years before moving to tight end and defensive end as a senior. He also played basketball and represented his school in shot put and javelin throwing. On his arrival at BYU, Freeland converted to offensive tackle but didn’t see the field until the middle of his freshman season. However, he ended up starting the last seven games and held up reasonably well, as he only allowed one sack. He didn’t begin his sophomore year as a starter, but ended up making a total of eight starts in 2020, during which he showed promise by not allowing a sack all year. In 2021 and 2022, Freeland started all 26 games and was twice named to Phil Steele’s all-Independent Conference first team. He was also a third team AP all-American in 2022. He soon made his first start due to a week four injury, and by the end of the year had started nine games. In 2024, he failed to earn a starting role and spent the first half of the season as a healthy scratch. He played in the last eight games, although he only played 23 offensive snaps, 22 of which were in the season finale. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets face off this weekend, and their seasons couldn’t be going in more opposite directions. Buffalo has won four straight games, and they are 7-1 overall for the season. The Jets, meanwhile, have lost four straight games, and they sit at just 2-7 overall. Where both teams are equal, though, is in the win column vs. other AFC East foes. The Jets have dropped games to both the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins this season, while the Bills had their only loss come at the hands of those Patriots. Neither Buffalo nor New York has a division win this season, something that both teams want to change on Sunday. How can the Bills overcome the Jets? Well, they’ll have to start by taking care of their own business, but they’ll also need to keep tabs on the Jets’ top players. Here are five Jets to watch this week against Buffalo. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Geno Smith The veteran has been solid in his second go-round with the Jets, as he’s thrown 12 touchdown passes against just three interceptions so far this season. Smith’s 100.5 quarterback rating is outstanding, as is his 67.5% completion rate on the year. However, he’s also taken a whopping 28 sacks for a league-leading 236 yards lost. If the Bills can win their matchups up front, Smith will hold the ball, and at 36 years old, he doesn’t have the mobility he once had. Smith was never a great runner, but he’s not someone I’d call elusive in the pocket. Buffalo should look to heat him up early in the game before giving him more simulated pressure looks as the game progresses. Speed up his clock to force him to make mistakes. He’ll hold the ball and take a sack over throwing an interception more often than not, so Buffalo’s defensive front needs to be ready to feast. RB Breece Hall The explosive runner has ten career 100-yard games on the ground, and two of those 100-yard games are against the Bills. Hall missed time this year with a quad injury, and he returned last week for the Jets’ 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. He carried 15 times for 61 yards in the game, which was his second-best output of the season.
